_comment: The one list of what forces a full PR run in CI (scripts/ci/affected.mjs reads it; docs/ops/ci.md explains it). Paths are anchored at the repository root; ** crosses directories, * does not. When more than one trigger matches, the most specific one is reported. extra_edges are dependencies the package.json files do not declare (relative imports and file reads across packages, found by scanning the tree): `from` depends on `to`, so a change to `to` also selects `from`. kind says whether the import is in shipped code (src) or only in tests (test); only the kinds in active_edge_kinds count, so dropping 'test' there narrows the selection to shipped-code couplings in one edit. Targets that are full-run triggers anyway (packages/core, packages/db, packages/test-guard) are not listed. CONTENT RULES (D#507 follow-up): the lists above say which files matter; these say when a file in them does not. metadata_only_keys: a package.json whose base and head differ ONLY in these keys (parsed JSON compared, not text) is neither a trigger, a package selection nor an e2e path; anything else, or a parse failure, keeps the path rule. standalone: a file that only needs its own run (it neither triggers nor selects a package). e2e_paths decide the workspace-e2e jobs alone: a full run forces the full unit and check scope, and e2e runs only when a changed file matches e2e_paths or the ci_workflow rule says the e2e job itself changed. ci_workflow: the one workflow file whose diff is read by content.

triggers.reason: the lockfile changes what every package resolves
root manifest: scripts, engines and the vitest and eslint versions every package uses
defines the workspace graph and the install overrides
root TypeScript config that the packages extend
defines which projects exist and how they run
root lint config applies to every package
the dev shell every job runs inside
pins the toolchain every job runs inside
a migration changes the schema every package's tests run against

CI and gate tooling, including this classifier, check.sh and the files it runs (scripts/lib/**, scripts/ci/vitest-projects.mjs, scripts/check-globalsetup-env.sh); the only narrowing is the standalone list below
generated files: a hand edit or a stale regeneration can break the web tests
the env manifest checked by the production build gate and the docs
the production build gate for the env manifest
rendered from the env manifest and compared with it by an apps/web test
imported by almost every package; owns the schema
its setup file is wired into every vitest project

ignore.reason: documentation (docs/ops/staging.md is a trigger, which wins)
archived material that nothing builds or tests

standalone.reason: a node test of one CI script: the node-test step of ci.yml runs it on every pull request, and nothing else reads a test file. NOT narrowed: affected.mjs, full-run-triggers.json, check.sh, scripts/lib/** and anything else CI executes stay full-run triggers via scripts/**

ci_workflow.test_step: Migration lint and secret scan tests
ci_workflow.reason: ci.yml is a full-run trigger and, when its diff touches anything outside the check job, an e2e trigger. A diff confined to the run line of the node-test step (the list of test files) is neither: that step runs on every pull request anyway. A diff confined to the check job is a full-run trigger but not an e2e one: the workspace-e2e job is a separate job with its own checkout. Any other workflow file is a full-run trigger and never an e2e one

e2e_paths.reason: the lockfile changes what the specs' app resolves
the workspace graph and install overrides the e2e job installs with
root manifest (a metadata-only edit is exempted before this list is read)
root TypeScript config that the app and the specs extend
the dev shell and the browsers the job runs with
pins the toolchain and the browsers the job runs with

the workspace shell is what the specs drive
the app the specs run against
